Container.Name: orchestrarr
Container.Overview: One dashboard for Plex, Sonarr, Radarr, Jellyseerr, qBittorrent and the rest of your media stack: playback, requests, queues and service health, with actions like approving requests and importing downloads. On first start Orchestrarr generates an API key and prints it once; read it with "docker logs orchestrarr" and sign in with it. Then add your services under Services, using your server's LAN address and each service's port.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Port for the dashboard. Change the host side if 4173 is taken.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Settings, service credentials and the generated API key. Keep this in appdata so it is backed up.

Config.Name: Demo mode
Config.Description: true shows fictional sample data instead of your services. Leave false to use your own stack.

Config.Name: Authentication
Config.Description: apikey: sign in with a key (generated on first start if empty below). basic: username and password. none: no sign-in, only for a trusted network.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: Optional. Leave empty and Orchestrarr generates one on first start and prints it in the logs. To choose your own: openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: Webhook secret
Config.Description: Optional shared secret for Sonarr, Radarr and Plex webhooks. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: Behind a proxy
Config.Description: true when Orchestrarr sits behind Cloudflare or a reverse proxy, so rate limits see each visitor's address.
